newsitem.title: NORWAY: Oslo Bourse ends higher on U.S. data, Orkla rally.
newsitem.headline: Oslo Bourse ends higher on U.S. data, Orkla rally.

text.p: The Oslo Bourse ended in positive territory on Thursday following weaker-than-expected U.S. May retail sales data and a surge in the share price of food-based conglomerate Orkla. The index closed 0.05 percent higher at 1,176.23 points in trade worth 1.1 billion crowns.
"We had been waiting for the U.S. data and this should give things a push here at home," a broker said.

Orkla's A share ended three percent, or 16 crowns, higher at 544 crowns after U.S. consumer products giant Procter & Gamble denied a media report that it would imminently move into the Norwegian detergents market.
Orkla A was the most traded stock at 161 million crowns.
Daily financial Dagens Naeringsliv reported this week that Procter & Gamble was planning to set up shop in Norway and that Orkla was bracing itself for a tough fight on its home turf.
Orkla's A stock tumbled 25 crowns on Tuesday to 548 crowns and an additional 20 crowns on Wednesday following the report.
"Procter & Gamble have no immediate plans to launch detergents in Norway right now," a spokeswoman for the U.S. group told Reuters.
